Book Review: “Travelling To Infinity”

By Mairi Hughes | Dec 17, 2020
travelling to infinity Photograph by Mairi Hughes.
One book which has been gathering dust on my shelf is “Travelling to Infinity” by Jane Hawking.
The book, an account of Jane and Stephen Hawking’s life together, was initially published in 1999. When it was made into a film (“The Theory of Everything”) in 2014, the book was re-released with an

...

e time to get into it!

A thorough timeline

Jane Hawking states that, while publishers chased her for an autobiography for a long time, it took her years of processing her marriage before she could put pen to paper.
The result, which is just shy of 500 pages, covers the highs and lows of the Hawkings’ marriage comprehensively.
It begins in 1962, when Stephen briefly attended St Albans High School For Girls.
The book takes readers through Jane and Stephen’s early romance as university students, and his diagnosis with motor neuron disease at the age of 21.
It covers their wedding and their travels as Stephen became a prominent academic. It also details their family life, with their three children.
Finally, it tells of their struggles as Stephen’s health declined.

A natural writer

Being an academic herself, with a PhD in mediaeval Spanish poetry, Jane Hawking’s writing is rich and descriptive.

Description

Soon to be a major motion picture, "Travelling to Infinity" is a poignant memoir by Jane Hawking, detailing her tumultuous marriage to the renowned physicist Stephen Hawking.

...

Jane's life became intertwined with that of physicist Stephen Hawking when they met at a party in 1962, leading to their engagement in 1964, despite the challenges his motor neurone disease presented. They married in 1965 and raised three children together. Jane authored her first autobiography, "Music to Move the Stars: A Life with Stephen," in 1999, which was later updated and retitled "Travelling to Infinity: My Life with Stephen" in 2009, coinciding with the release of the acclaimed film "The Theory of Everything." In 2015, she shared insights about her life in a feature on BBC

...

Jane and Stephen In the summer of 1962, Jane Hawking reflects on her early life experiences that subtly intertwined with Stephen Hawking’s. Their paths crossed during their time at St Albans High School for Girls, where Jane noticed Stephen as a peculiar boy with floppy hair in a neighboring classroom.
